title: What is your process to generate animations?
author: DoomGuyGraphics
selftext:
I am making a 2d top-down game with 8 directional movement.

Has anyone succeeded in making animations with AI for this setup? If yes, can you share your workflow and some of your content? 

Thanks!

comments.author: VikingKingMoore
comments.body: Create an idle 1 or 2 frame. Gather references of how the 8 way should look and Draw out the other frames manually to get a consistent image. it really doesn’t take that long if you use a program like asprite.

comments.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
comments.body: I’m doing sidescroller but I think both pixel-lab/aseprite and retrodiffusion do this well. I was using retro but not am mainly using pixellab. It’s so nice having things generate right inside aseprite.

replies.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
replies.body: You can use pixel lab as a plugin in aseprite. When you generate something it does it right inside aseprite. It’s really nice.

replies.author: ButcherPetesWagon
replies.body: You just blew my mind friend

replies.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
replies.body: I bet you’ll dig it. I’m using it for sidescroller/platformer but it actually seems built for more of an overhead thing. DM me if you need help.

comments.author: Darknessborn
comments.body: I've tried a bunch and think pixellab is the best so far, does 8dir sprites well, animates them, has map building tools, and even an aseprite-like editor built in to polish your assets

replies.author: AdrianRWalker
replies.body: The Aseprite plugin is the best. Being able to kick off images and then edit them quickly is a solid advantage in workflow.

comments.author: Ukatyushas
comments.body:
I am testing a 3d sprite workflow.

1. Create concept art with nano banana pro
2. Use concept art to create mesh in tripo
3. If needed, cleanup Mesh in blender with quad remesher and manually etc, and/or use Modiff to finalize textures 
4. Upload mesh to Mixamo to generate rig. Might need to adjust rig manually.
5. Download any base animations from mixamo import into blender (I haven't explored generated animations in depth)
6. Use python script to render the sprites using blender

This gives you high amounts of control over visual direction

replies.author: webfugitive
replies.body: This is what I'm trying to do, but any idea how would you use something like Modly in this workflow? I can't seem to get the mesh to go into Mixamo.

replies.author: Ukatyushas
replies.body:
Idk about modly. I'm assuming you have a mesh in blender, then you can export it from blender as a .obj to upload to mixamo. Then you download the rigged mesh and/or animations as an fbx and import into blender.

video with example: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=68pOKXxJiq8

comments.author: Appropriate-Value610
comments.body: I’m interested on this too, especially if animation can be done mostly with Claude Code or any free tools…

comments.author: Vast_Emu_2346
comments.body: Honestly by hand or via code

comments.author: SubstantialOption122
comments.body: for 8-directional sprites i'd generate a base character in one pose then use a sprite sheet workflow in comfyui with ControlNet to lock the pose per direction. you can also script rotation transforms in Aseprite for quicker iteration. Mage Space at [mage.space](http://mage.space) works for the inital character generation step.

comments.author: macuseri686
comments.body:
Just using a normal AI model like Nano Banana wont work for assets such as spritesheets, because AI models like nano banana cant output transparency, and image models alone have no understanding of animation.

That gap is actually why I built GameLab Studio [https://gamelabstudio.co](https://gamelabstudio.co) . It’s designed for game assets and it’ll generate consistent pixel-art sprites, animations and full transparent bg spritesheets for anything.

https://i.redd.it/h8ly86k4blxg1.gif

Gamelabs Studio MCP plugs right into your agent like Cursor, to enable rapid iteration right in your code editor

[https://gamelabstudio.co/blog/mcp-setup-guide](https://gamelabstudio.co/blog/mcp-setup-guide)

It also enforces consistency across scale, palette, and angles, by using already generated angles of the same asset for reference, so you don’t end up with “AI asset soup” during prototyping.

We also have a seamless tileable edge-aware texture generation model
